references.text: Moses exhorts the people not to fear; this same encouragement is given here at Sinai.
The exhortation 'do not be afraid' is repeated by Moses when Israel is about to enter the Promised Land.
Moses speaks to the people, telling them not to fear their enemies, for the Lord fights for them.
Joshua gives the same exhortation to the people: 'Do not be afraid and do not be terrified.'
A similar situation where the people are exhorted not to fear but to look for the Lord's salvation.
The word of the Lord through Isaiah: 'Do not be afraid, for I am with you.'
The Lord assures Israel not to fear, for He has redeemed them.
David expresses trust in the Lord's salvation without fear of enemies.
The psalm speaks of not fearing even if the earth shakes, for God is our refuge.
Hebrews refers to the crossing of the Red Sea by faith.
Paul speaks of God's salvation and deliverance from danger.
The psalm recalls how the Lord saved Israel at the Red Sea from their enemies.
A clear allusion and theological parallel: Jehoshaphat is urged to stand firm and see the Lord's salvation, just as Moses did at the Red Sea.
